feed.title: Thoughts on a network policy for quantum-vulnerable UTXOs (long-exposure quantum attacks)

entry.title: Thoughts on a network policy for quantum-vulnerable UTXOs (long-exposure quantum attacks)
entry.summary:
Securing assets over an indefinite period is a central objective for users of Bitcoin, enabling them to retain and utilize funds at any future time without fear of confiscation or theft. While this goal is generally achieved within the current system, certain Unspent Transaction Outputs (UTXOs) are exposed to risk should cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) become viable. This development could render some existing UTXOs susceptible to unauthorized access, representing a potential security challenge.
However, this concern does not extend universally across all UTXOs, nor is there a comprehensive remedy that fundamentally alters the limitations imposed by the emergence of CRQCs. No proposals exist that can completely eliminate the risk posed by quantum computing to vulnerable UTXOs. As a result, attention shifts toward partial solutions or mitigations that target the most significant risks arising from this technological advancement.
Identifying the precise problem to address is essential before formulating solutions. Not all users currently possess quantum-vulnerable UTXOs, and understanding whose interests are at stake and what specific threats must be countered guides the development of effective responses. In other domains, proactive communication and encouraging users to upgrade their cryptographic protections and keys represent standard preventive measures. Establishing consensus on the nature and significance of the problem lays the foundation for pragmatic strategies that mitigate the impact of quantum computing threats within the Bitcoin ecosystem.
